novelty.reasoning: The candidate equation extends the classical quadratic-drag baseline dv_dt = -(drag/mass)*v*|v| with several additional physically-motivated but non-standard composite terms. Term-by-term: (1) The drag term now uses air-relative velocity (v + headwind sinusoid in position) and multiplies by a Reynolds-number correction factor (1 + air_density_lapse*(v - reference_velocity)). Individually, quadratic drag with relative wind and velocity-dependent drag coefficients are known physical concepts, but the specific composite form with a spatially sinusoidal headwind field embedded inside the |.| structure is unusual. (2) The rolling friction term uses tanh(v/velocity_scale) as a smooth sign regularizer (a known trick) multiplied by a temperature-dependent factor (1 + brake_heating_sensitivity*brake_temperature), which is coupled to a separate ODE for contact temperature with frictional heating and Newtonian cooling. (3) A position-dependent gravitational term from sinusoidal track undulations (track_slope_amplitude*g*sin(k*x + phase)). Each individual mechanism (quadratic drag, temperature-modulated friction, undulating slope, wind profile) has textbook precedent, but the COMPLETE combined multi-physics ODE system—coupling velocity, position-dependent wind and grade, and a dynamically evolving contact temperature that feeds back into friction—does not appear as a single closed-form equation in any textbook or public reference. An LLM could not recite this exact composite formula; it represents a specific engineered combination whose particular functional couplings (e.g., temperature-dependent friction coefficient with the specific heating law, Reynolds correction linear in (v - v_ref), spatial sinusoids inside the drag and slope terms) could only be identified through data-driven inference. This goes well beyond simple recall of the classical baseline.
